task_packet.capability_success_condition: Deliver one coherent Phase 50A pull request implementing and proving all nine capabilities authorized by merged ADR-049Q §13.1: (a) provider-neutral PostgreSQL persistence behind the existing unchanged synchronous StorageAdapter semantic seam; (b) canonical provider-neutral migrations; (c) local/development/operator-grade non-production integration proof; (d) append-only, append-ordered audit persistence with per-estate hash chaining and a retrievable tail; (e) ordinary PostgreSQL export and restore with a documented exercise; (f) rollback for failed migration and failed admission transaction; (g) idempotency; (h) concurrency and isolation that re-establish single-writer-equivalent ordering; and (i) provider-replacement proof by restoring into a second distinct conforming PostgreSQL host with semantics and audit chain intact. The synchronous/asynchronous boundary must be explicit and fail closed: keep StorageAdapter method signatures and EstateStore/recall/audit semantics unchanged; use an asynchronous PostgreSQL host boundary that opens a database transaction, establishes per-estate serialization, loads a transaction-scoped synchronous StorageAdapter-conforming snapshot/session, runs one bounded callback, verifies immutable append prefixes and audit-chain integrity, persists the deterministic delta atomically, and commits before returning success. No fire-and-forget writes, no fake synchronous network I/O, and no success before durable commit. Identical retries may be idempotent only when the canonical payload is identical; an existing immutable id with conflicting payload must raise an integrity error and roll back. Canonical migrations and domain persistence must contain no Railway or other provider-specific semantics. The proof harness must use two separate local PostgreSQL server instances, source and replacement, without external provider access or committed credentials. Directory entries in allowed_paths authorize descendants only; forbidden_paths wins on any overlap.

required_tests: Run npm ci, npm run build, npm run typecheck, npm test, npm run control-plane:validate, npm run control-plane:test, and git diff --check.
Run a dedicated Phase 50A PostgreSQL test command against two clean, separately addressable local PostgreSQL server instances started by the checked-in non-production harness.
Run the existing StorageAdapter conformance scenarios against a transaction-scoped PostgreSQL-backed adapter session without weakening the InMemoryStorage or JsonlStorage cases.
Prove unknown ids return undefined or empty collections rather than throwing.
Prove actor, estate, keyring, assertion, and receipt upserts keep the latest canonical version by primary id.
Prove transitions and audit events remain append-only and append-ordered, with database constraints or triggers refusing mutation.
Prove per-estate audit tails and previous_audit_hash links survive cold reload and verify with the existing AuditLog verifier.
Prove a complete admit plus recall flow is atomically durable only after the host transaction commits, and that a forced failure rolls back every row from the attempted operation.
Prove an identical retry is idempotent and creates no duplicate immutable record; prove conflicting reuse of an immutable id fails and rolls back.
Prove two concurrent same-estate operations serialize without lost updates, duplicate append positions, chain forks, or silent drops; verify the final chain and all receipts.
Prove concurrent operations on different estates do not leak or cross-contaminate state.
Apply canonical migrations from empty database to current version and prove repeated migrate is idempotent.
Exercise migration rollback in non-production and prove the documented rollback behavior before re-applying successfully.

Populate the source host, perform ordinary PostgreSQL export, restore into the separate replacement host, compare canonical state, verify the audit chain identically, cold-load the estate, and execute a successful governed recall.
Verify generated build/type artifacts are reproducible but are not committed.
required_negative_tests: Database unavailable, connection interrupted, transaction aborted, or migration version mismatch fails closed and returns no successful durable operation.
A malformed or partial canonical row, broken audit hash, non-prefix immutable history, duplicate append position, or conflicting immutable id is rejected rather than served or silently repaired.
Direct UPDATE or DELETE of transition, transition-receipt, recall-receipt, or audit-event immutable history is refused.
A concurrent chain-tail race cannot create two children of the same previous_audit_hash.
Restore with missing rows, changed canonical payload, or broken audit chain is detected and the restored estate is quarantined/refused from normal service.
No code path falls back to InMemoryStorage or JsonlStorage after PostgreSQL uncertainty while reporting success.
The implementation must stop rather than alter StorageAdapter signatures or estate semantics to make PostgreSQL easier.
required_no_leak_checks: No secret, credential, password, token, certificate, connection string, live endpoint, account/project id, region, provider topology, or production environment value is committed.

Test credentials are fixed local-only values confined to the non-production compose/workflow harness and are clearly unusable outside it.
No local absolute path, home directory, cloud workspace identifier, or generated .run artifact is committed.
No sibling repository content is copied into the implementation and no hidden subagent contribution is accepted without disclosure.

concerns.location: .github/workflows/phase-50a-postgres-conformance.yml:31,83,89; Actions run 30559231765 / job 90927625048 / step Install dependencies
concerns.description: The required remote proof never reaches any substantive step: npm ci fails E401 fetching private @0xhoneyjar/loa-hounfour because the workflow grants no packages: read permission, setup-node does not configure the GitHub Packages registry/scope, and npm ci receives no ephemeral NODE_AUTH_TOKEN. Every build, test, two-host, and artifact step is skipped. The bounded proof-harness correction is the established GitHub Packages pattern: packages: read, setup-node registry-url https://npm.pkg.github.com with scope @0xhoneyjar, and NODE_AUTH_TOKEN from the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN only on npm ci; also verify that the package's Actions access grants or inherits access for loa-straylight. Never commit a credential. The auditor token lacks read:packages, so package-level access could not be independently queried.

withEstateSession accepts a generic callback result and commits immediately after body(session) without settling or refusing a returned Promise. An independent PostgreSQL probe returned committed:true and durably wrote one actor row, then the callback Promise rejected with 'late async callback failure'. This violates callback-error rollback and commit-before-success. The bounded correction is to settle or explicitly refuse PromiseLike callback results before session close, persistence, and COMMIT, with rejection rolling back.

Unique-violation idempotency classifies an existing immutable ID by canonical payload alone, despite selecting promoted columns. An independent direct-SQL probe inserted the same transition ID and payload under estate:wrong-promoted-column; a session for the canonical estate then returned committed:true and persisted {inserted:0,idempotent:1}, while zero rows were visible to that estate. Idempotent equality must cover the complete immutable durable row: promoted estate_id, append_position, audit hash/parent columns where present, and canonical payload; any mismatch must throw and roll back.

The migration ledger stores only version and applied_at, and migrate trusts an existing version without binding it to the shipped SQL. A changed 0001 file can therefore be silently treated as applied. The bounded correction is to record an immutable canonical migration checksum/digest and verify every applied version against the current shipped migration before skipping it or serving the schema.

Complete generated-tree/package reproducibility is not established. clean:types plus build emits 12 untracked PostgreSQL declarations, and npm pack --dry-run runs prepare and includes all 12 because files includes dist-types/. No public root/host/runtime declaration references PostgreSQL, so there is no dangling consumer-visible reference, but internal-only status does not make the intentionally committed dist-types artifact equal to the complete generated or packed tree. The workflow checks only tracked-file equality and explicitly blesses the extra files. Resolution must choose one coherent contract: if these declarations are package artifacts, revising the packet is required because dist-types/ is forbidden; otherwise the authorized build/package/workflow surface must exclude them and verify exact complete-tree and packed-content reproducibility.

The pull_request path filter omits src/straylight/index.ts and both Phase 50A documents even though no-leak-and-neutrality.test.ts reads those exact files. A change to the public-export guard or proof/runbook leak surface can therefore bypass this workflow. Add those three authorized test-input paths to the trigger set.

concerns.description: Promise-like refusal still reads a custom thenable's `then` getter twice. `isThenable` reads it at line 354, then `absorbSettlement` reads it again at line 377 despite the line 345-348 claim that the first read is reused. An independent stateful-thenable probe made the first getter access return a bound `then` for a delayed-rejecting Promise and the second access throw. The operation correctly refused with `async_callback_unsupported` and rolled back to zero durable actor rows, but the getter was accessed twice and the later underlying rejection surfaced through `unhandledRejection`. This fails the required custom-thenable/no-unhandled-rejection closure. Capture the callable `then` exactly once and invoke that captured function with the original receiver, then add a stateful getter plus delayed-rejection regression.

Every schema-version check runs ledger-shape and trigger DDL, including `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, inside the estate transaction before the per-estate locks. That DDL acquires a relation lock held until the estate callback commits, globally coupling unrelated estates. A two-process probe held estate A's synchronous callback for 4000 ms; estate B used a different estate id but reached its callback only 4021 ms later. `pg_stat_activity` showed B waiting on `Lock/relation` at the ALTER TABLE. With B's statement timeout set to 500 ms, the unrelated estate failed with `transaction_aborted: canceling statement due to statement timeout`. This is a patch-introduced concurrency regression and contradicts the documented claim that different estates never contend. Ledger creation/upgrade and trigger installation must occur in the migration/initialization path; steady-state checksum verification must be read-only. Add a cross-process test that holds one estate callback and proves a second estate reaches its callback without waiting or timing out.

The workflow now contains the three missing trigger paths, but the claimed anti-drift assertion is not anti-vacuous. Both tests hardcode the same three strings and merely check that each appears in the no-leak source and workflow. If the no-leak suite later reads a fourth fixed path outside the existing globs, this test remains green while the workflow omits it. Derive the complete relevant input set from one declared manifest or otherwise compare the no-leak suite's actual fixed inputs against the workflow path set, and add a mutation proving an omitted new input fails.

The operator runbook still says an uncertain retry is safe when the canonical payload is identical. Finding 3 established that payload equality is insufficient: the complete immutable durable row, including promoted estate, position, audit hash, parent hash/key, and identity, must match. Update the runbook condition so it does not direct operators to treat a same-payload promoted-column mismatch as an idempotent retry.

The proof document reports 14 patch-only changed paths, but 8602a2c753b2ad873175bc227e091a06da19a663..212e9ee769a31d69e0c0d0b508465b12d23a9a4d changes 16 paths. The prose lists 14 non-document paths and then adds this document and the runbook. State the total as 16, or explicitly distinguish 14 implementation/test paths plus 2 documents.

concerns.description: The unreadable-then refusal formats the callback getter exception through describe(), which exposes an ordinary Error message in the public PostgresUnavailableError. If conversion to string itself throws, describe() lets that exception escape; classify() invokes describe() again, and the exact original object reaches the caller instead of the bounded async_callback_unsupported error. A local Vitest observation at this exact SHA recorded one getter access, zero durable actor rows, session_closed on the escaped session, and zero unhandled rejections, but caughtIsGetterException=true and caughtIsBoundedError=false. Rollback and invalidation are correct; the public exception boundary is not.

Loaded-prefix idempotency still compares only canonical payload. classifyExistingAppend() runs before claimPosition(), has no offered append_position, and counts a loaded row as idempotent whenever immutable id and payload match. A local dense-prefix observation with a filler at position 1 and the target id/payload at position 2 returned committed=true and persisted={inserted:0,idempotent:1}. That contradicts the stated complete immutable durable-row equality contract, including promoted append_position. This is separate from prefix-movement detection, which passed.

The current declared input set is covered and the eight estate-domain workflow paths are present, but the required anti-drift mutation contract is not enforced. Deleting src/straylight/storage/postgres from the authoritative declaration left all 33 focused tests green; weakening the extractor with slice(1) left all 19 contract tests green; and a renamed COVERAGE_DEBT set applied during extraction accepted a real uncovered declared input while all 33 tests passed. Positive controls for adding a new uncovered input, removing each of the eight triggers, and attempting the modeled undeclared by-name read do fail and name the relevant path. This is a proof/test-harness defect, not evidence that a trigger is currently absent.

The current three ThenReadOutcome variants are handled, but TypeScript exhaustiveness is not enforced. The code uses two independent if branches and treats every remaining variant as not-thenable; adding a fourth variant passes npm run typecheck and can fall through to session.close(), persistence, and commit. The implementation report's claim that disabling the unreadable branch fails at compile time is therefore not supported by the exact source.

concerns.description: TECHNICAL R2 REOPENED. offerPosition resets to 1 in every transaction and treats a session-local offer ordinal as the historical durable append position. A full estate-prefix replay converges, while partial, reordered, sparse, and duplicated probes refuse with zero partial durability, but requiring all historical operations to be replayed is not operation-level idempotency and does not close the cross-estate boundary. The complete-row comparator does include position and chain columns and direct mismatches roll back, but the incoming position and estate authority supplied to it are semantically unsound. A correction needs a trusted expected-placement and session-estate binding; a counter that restarts per session cannot establish historical position.

Deliver ONE fresh Phase 50A architecture-correction pull request that replaces two unsound abstractions with closed designs, on a FRESH branch phase-50a-r2-r3-architecture-correction branched from rejected SHA f1b5f0f3924eb4c8624c8b2efb1f3072fbfa92f4 (used ONLY as inspectable substrate, never as merge evidence) and opened as a FRESH pull request against main. PR #124, branch phase-50a-rejection-remediation, and every earlier rejected branch or SHA must never be reopened, amended, extended, or cited as merge evidence. R1 (bounded callback-thenability refusal that publishes nothing of the caller's exception) and R4 (assertNever totality barrier over ThenReadOutcome) are independently CLOSED and must be preserved exactly, with their pinning tests intact. Every other previously accepted behavior must remain green: transaction atomicity, commit-before-success, rollback and session invalidation, callable-thenable settlement absorption, migration checksum enforcement, append-only constraints, audit-chain verification, same-estate serialization, cross-estate progress, two-host export/restore/replacement, provider neutrality, package reproducibility under the internal-only exclusion contract, the synchronous StorageAdapter shape, and the no-leak checks.

R2 — REPLACE THE OFFERED-ORDINAL ABSTRACTION WITH A SEPARATED, ORDER-INDEPENDENT MODEL. Delete the session/callback-local offered append ordinal entirely (offerPosition and the offered* counters). It is unsound at the root: StorageAdapter.appendTransition / upsertTransitionReceipt / upsertRecallReceipt / appendAuditEvent supply NO append position, so no caller-supplied append position exists and none may be invented; a counter that restarts every transaction cannot establish a historical durable position. The replacement design must separate two independent concerns that the rejected code conflated.

(1) CALLER-CONTROLLED IMMUTABLE EQUALITY. Two writes are the same durable write exactly when the immutable primary id matches AND every CALLER-CONTROLLED immutable field matches: the canonical payload (which carries the record's own id), the record's own estate_id, and for audit events the caller-supplied chain fields audit_hash and previous_audit_hash together with its normalized previous_audit_hash_key ('' must never be conflated with NULL). append_position is NOT caller-controlled and must NOT appear in this comparison; comparing it against an invented ordinal is exactly what falsely refused a byte-identical replay of an independently committed operation. This comparison must be computed identically by the in-snapshot classifier in session.ts and the live-row classifier in persist.ts, over ONE shared declaration of the caller-controlled column set, pinned structurally by a test so the two cannot drift. persist.ts must keep binding every durable column it INSERTs (including append_position) while comparing only the caller-controlled subset, and must separately check the live row's placement per (3).

(2) SESSION-ESTATE BINDING. The host locks exactly one estate and loads exactly that estate's snapshot, so the session must be constructed bound to that estate id and every append-only write must FIRST require record.estate_id to equal the session's bound estate. A record naming any other estate is refused as an integrity violation with a distinct bounded reason and rolls the transaction back — never classified idempotent, never committed. This closes the hole where records owned by one estate, replayed through a session opened and locked for a different estate, committed with inserted 0 and idempotent 3 because promoted estate equality was checked against the record instead of the session's estate authority. Estate authority is the session's, not the record's. Update the three internal probe-session construction sites (load.ts assertChainIntact, portability.ts, host.ts) accordingly. The PostgresAdapterSession constructor is INTERNAL (not re-exported from src/straylight/index.ts, no package subpath, declarations pruned from the package), so binding an estate to it is not a public-contract change and must not be treated as one; the public StorageAdapter interface, EstateStore, AuditLog, and recall APIs stay byte-unchanged and synchronous.

(3) STORE-ASSIGNED PLACEMENT INTEGRITY. Placement is the store's, verified against the store's own invariants rather than against any caller claim: the per-estate dense-prefix invariant already asserted at load (assertLoadedIntegrity / assertDensePositions) and re-asserted before persist (assertPrefixUnchanged), plus the shipped database constraints CHECK (append_position >= 1), UNIQUE (estate_id, append_position), UNIQUE (estate_id, previous_audit_hash_key), and the audit genesis CHECK. Classification must validate that the STORED position of a matched row is consistent with those invariants, and must refuse when it is not. Only a FRESH immutable id receives the next position (loaded dense maximum for that estate plus one); a converging existing id consumes NO position and creates no duplicate.

ORDER INDEPENDENCE AND PINNED OUTCOMES. Because no counter participates, existing-id classification is a pure function of the offered record, the session's bound estate, and the stored rows — independent of callback ordering, of session-local ordering, and of how many earlier appends this session made. Pin each of the following as an explicit, named, asserted outcome, in both the in-snapshot and the live-row path where both apply: a FULL faithful operation retry converges with zero duplicates and zero new positions; a PARTIAL operation retry that re-offers only a subset of an earlier operation's records converges on exactly the records it offers and is NOT required to re-offer historical records — per-record convergence is the adapter contract, and operation-level idempotency must not be redefined as whole-estate-prefix replay; REORDERED and DUPLICATED offers of byte-identical records converge identically regardless of offer order; a SPARSE or gapped history is refused at load and quarantined rather than served; the SAME immutable id under a DIFFERENT estate is refused by the session-estate binding, and a record whose id already exists under another estate is never treated as convergence; any PROMOTED- or CALLER-FIELD MISMATCH on an existing id (payload, estate, audit_hash, previous_audit_hash, normalized key) raises the immutable-id-conflict integrity error and rolls back; CONCURRENT VISIBILITY — a row committed by another transaction between this session's load and its write is invisible to the snapshot, surfaces as a unique violation at insert, and is classified against the live row by the same caller-controlled column set inside its savepoint. ZERO PARTIAL DURABILITY is absolute: for any refusal the transaction rolls back and no row from the attempted operation survives; success is reported only after COMMIT. Convergences must remain observable in the persist result rather than looking like a callback that did nothing.

R3 — REPLACE THE HEURISTIC PROOF WITH AN INDEPENDENTLY AUTHORITATIVE CLOSED COVERAGE MODEL. Remove source-extraction-derived authority and every accepted-gap or exception mechanism. No proof may derive its authority from the extractor it validates, and there must be no exception list of any kind — not a renamed one, not an empty one. Adopt a FIXED CHECKED-IN MANIFEST of the proof's input roots and globs, committed under tests/phase-50a/ or scripts/phase-50a/ as data, and make it the SINGLE declaration: the no-leak/neutrality suite must READ ITS INPUTS FROM the manifest instead of restating them, so there is one declaration and nothing to extract. Prefer BROAD roots such as src/straylight/** over fragile named-file enumeration, because a broad root also covers files that do not exist yet and therefore cannot be defeated by deleting, renaming, or adding a declaration. Coverage must be proven by BOUNDED SEMANTIC comparison between the manifest and a STRUCTURAL parse of the workflow's own raw bytes: parse on.pull_request.paths and on.workflow_dispatch from the checked-in YAML through a bounded parser with its own negative tests (indentation, interleaved comments, block termination, nested keys, quoting variants, list-item shapes), and reject the rejected suite's fragile fixed-offset text-slice approach. Neither side may be derived from the other: the manifest is checked-in data, the workflow set is parsed from the workflow file, and the comparison is manifest against parsed workflow. The required set of uncovered manifest inputs must be EMPTY, with no list to append an exception to. The model must mechanically catch, each with its own asserted failing mutation: extractor replacement or reintroduction of any indirection that could synthesize a covered path; deletion of a declared input; filtering or truncation applied during declaration or comparison; renaming of a declaration, marker, block, or constant; a VACUOUS declaration — the manifest must be non-empty and every declared root must resolve to at least one real tracked file, and every real tracked file under a declared root must be inside the manifest so a declared root cannot be narrowed while files remain; and removal of any workflow trigger, including workflow_dispatch. The manifest file itself and the proof files that consume it must be workflow trigger inputs, so a change to the coverage model cannot merge without running the proof.

REMOTE PROOF — EXACT-HEAD GIT IDENTITY. Update the workflow so an EXACT 40-hex head SHA is explicitly checked out and asserted before any substantive step: derive the target SHA (workflow_dispatch input on manual runs, github.event.pull_request.head.sha on pull-request runs), validate it against ^[0-9a-f]{40}$, pass it as the actions/checkout ref, and then assert in a dedicated early step that git rev-parse HEAD equals that exact SHA, failing closed on any mismatch before build, typecheck, tests, suites, proof, or artifact verification run. A synthetic pull-request merge commit is NOT sufficient identity evidence even when its tree is byte-identical to the audited head; a byte-identical tree supports runtime-content coverage only. Preserve the existing pull_request proof path and add or use a bounded workflow_dispatch exact-head path as needed. The completion report must not restate an exact-head claim the evidence does not support.

fixed_executor_contract.mandate: REPLACE spawnSync process control. spawnSync must not appear in the production launch path in any form — not as the primary mechanism, not as a fallback, not behind a flag, and not as an injectable default. The replacement is a finite, fully enumerated Node 22 / Linux design; it is a REPLACEMENT of the process-control architecture, not a patch layered over the old one.
required_design: LAUNCH PRIMITIVE: node:child_process spawn (async), with shell:false stated explicitly, a fixed executable string and a fixed argv ARRAY per entry. No string-command form, no shell interpolation, no argument splitting, no command-word parsing anywhere.

BOUNDED TREE: every launch is detached into its OWN process group (detached: true, so the child becomes group leader and its descendants inherit that group), or an equivalent mechanism that yields one bounded, addressable tree per entry. The group identity must be captured from the live child (its pid as group id) and recorded, so the harness always knows exactly which tree it must account for.

SERIAL SCHEDULE: the same closed, literal, 12-entry schedule of { label, file, args, timeout_ms } in the same order, awaited strictly one at a time. It is never loaded, generated, templated, filtered, reordered or extended at runtime. Entry 1 remains npm ci --ignore-scripts and the explicit unauthenticated build remains its own later entry.

NO INTERPRETATION: no parser of any kind, no dynamic configuration loading, no dynamic code evaluation, no environment-driven or argument-driven command construction, and no recognition of workflow content.

TIMEOUT AS TREE TERMINATION: the harness itself owns the clock (it must NOT delegate the timeout to the launch primitive's own timeout option, whose kill reaches the direct child only). When timeout_ms lapses it signals the WHOLE GROUP with a terminating signal, waits a FIXED grace period, then escalates to an uncatchable signal to the WHOLE GROUP.

VERIFY BEFORE RECEIPT: after escalation the harness must VERIFY (a) the direct child was reaped — its exit or signal was actually observed, not assumed — and (b) the group is ABSENT, by a liveness probe of the group that must report gone. Only then may the receipt be written and the refusal returned. Verification must never be inferred from the mere passage of time.

FAIL CLOSED ON UNPROVEN CONTAINMENT: if reaping is not observed, or the group's absence cannot be established within the bounded verification window, the harness returns its OWN distinct containment-failure refusal and exits nonzero. Unproven containment is never reported as a plain timeout, never as success, and never silently ignored.

SIX DISTINCT OUTCOME CLASSES: nonzero exit, ordinary signal death, timeout, spawn failure, termination failure (signalling the group itself failed) and containment failure (the tree could not be proven gone). Each has its own refusal code, its own receipt fields and its own envelope line, checked in a stated precedence order. No pair may collapse, and a null status must never fall through an exit-code comparison as success.

NO SUCCESSOR, NO SURVIVOR: on any failure the harness launches ZERO later entries and leaves ZERO surviving descendants. Successor suppression alone is explicitly NOT containment; both properties are required and both are separately proven.

GATE ORDER PRESERVED AND EXTENDED: (1) hash the wrapper's RAW BYTES and require the pinned literal digest, hashing before any decoding; (2) require PHASE_50A_EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA to be exactly 40 lowercase hex; (3) require PHASE_50A_NPM_TOKEN present and non-blank and capture it ONCE; (4) launch the fixed git rev-parse HEAD identity probe — the only launch permitted before the gate completes, itself group-bounded, recorded as a probe and never counted as a schedule launch; (5) require observed HEAD to equal the expected SHA exactly; (6) only then run the schedule. A failure at any of 1-5 launches ZERO schedule commands. No fallback, no shortened schedule, and no refusal path that exits zero.

IDENTITY BANNER before the first schedule launch, carrying wrapper digest, executor digest, expected and observed head, schedule length, the authenticated entry label, and the containment parameters (grace period and verification window). It states no credential value.

DETERMINISTIC RECEIPTS: one receipt per ATTEMPTED command in attempt order, carrying ordinal, label, file, exact argv, status, signal, and the outcome class plus explicit containment fields (group signalled, escalated, reaped, group verified absent). No timestamp, no duration, no hostname, no absolute path, no environment value, no pid — so two runs of the same schedule produce byte-identical receipt text and no credential or machine detail can reach the log through a receipt.

NODE BUILTINS ONLY, because the executor runs BEFORE npm ci. Its own location comes from import.meta.dirname / import.meta.filename. The declaration file scripts/phase-50a/fixed-proof-executor.d.mts must be updated to match the new exported surface exactly.

fixed_executor_contract.mandate: REPLACE spawnSync process control. spawnSync must not appear in the production launch path in any form — not as the primary mechanism, not as a fallback, not behind a flag, and not as an injectable default. The replacement is a finite, fully enumerated Node 22 / Linux design; it is a REPLACEMENT of the process-control architecture, not a patch layered over the old one.
required_design: LAUNCH PRIMITIVE: node:child_process spawn (async), with shell:false stated explicitly, a fixed executable string and a fixed argv ARRAY per entry. No string-command form, no shell interpolation, no argument splitting, no command-word parsing anywhere.

BOUNDED TREE: every launch is detached into its OWN process group (detached: true, so the child becomes group leader and its descendants inherit that group), or an equivalent mechanism that yields one bounded, addressable tree per entry. The group identity must be captured from the live child (its pid as group id) and recorded, so the harness always knows exactly which tree it must account for.

SERIAL SCHEDULE: the same closed, literal, 12-entry schedule of { label, file, args, timeout_ms } in the same order, awaited strictly one at a time. It is never loaded, generated, templated, filtered, reordered or extended at runtime. Entry 1 remains npm ci --ignore-scripts and the explicit unauthenticated build remains its own later entry.

NO INTERPRETATION: no parser of any kind, no dynamic configuration loading, no dynamic code evaluation, no environment-driven or argument-driven command construction, and no recognition of workflow content.

TIMEOUT AS TREE TERMINATION: the harness itself owns the clock (it must NOT delegate the timeout to the launch primitive's own timeout option, whose kill reaches the direct child only). When timeout_ms lapses it signals the WHOLE GROUP with a terminating signal, waits a FIXED grace period, then escalates to an uncatchable signal to the WHOLE GROUP.

VERIFY BEFORE RECEIPT: after escalation the harness must VERIFY (a) the direct child was reaped — its exit or signal was actually observed, not assumed — and (b) the group is ABSENT, by a liveness probe of the group that must report gone. Only then may the receipt be written and the refusal returned. Verification must never be inferred from the mere passage of time.

FAIL CLOSED ON UNPROVEN CONTAINMENT: if reaping is not observed, or the group's absence cannot be established within the bounded verification window, the harness returns its OWN distinct containment-failure refusal and exits nonzero. Unproven containment is never reported as a plain timeout, never as success, and never silently ignored.

SIX DISTINCT OUTCOME CLASSES: nonzero exit, ordinary signal death, timeout, spawn failure, termination failure (signalling the group itself failed) and containment failure (the tree could not be proven gone). Each has its own refusal code, its own receipt fields and its own envelope line, checked in a stated precedence order. No pair may collapse, and a null status must never fall through an exit-code comparison as success.

NO SUCCESSOR, NO SURVIVOR: on any failure the harness launches ZERO later entries and leaves ZERO surviving descendants. Successor suppression alone is explicitly NOT containment; both properties are required and both are separately proven.

GATE ORDER PRESERVED AND EXTENDED: (1) hash the wrapper's RAW BYTES and require the pinned literal digest, hashing before any decoding; (2) require PHASE_50A_EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA to be exactly 40 lowercase hex; (3) require PHASE_50A_NPM_TOKEN present and non-blank and capture it ONCE; (4) launch the fixed git rev-parse HEAD identity probe — the only launch permitted before the gate completes, itself group-bounded, recorded as a probe and never counted as a schedule launch; (5) require observed HEAD to equal the expected SHA exactly; (6) only then run the schedule. A failure at any of 1-5 launches ZERO schedule commands. No fallback, no shortened schedule, and no refusal path that exits zero.

IDENTITY BANNER before the first schedule launch, carrying wrapper digest, executor digest, expected and observed head, schedule length, the authenticated entry label, and the containment parameters (grace period and verification window). It states no credential value.

DETERMINISTIC RECEIPTS: one receipt per ATTEMPTED command in attempt order, carrying ordinal, label, file, exact argv, status, signal, and the outcome class plus explicit containment fields (group signalled, escalated, reaped, group verified absent). No timestamp, no duration, no hostname, no absolute path, no environment value, no pid — so two runs of the same schedule produce byte-identical receipt text and no credential or machine detail can reach the log through a receipt.

NODE BUILTINS ONLY, because the executor runs BEFORE npm ci. Its own location comes from import.meta.dirname / import.meta.filename. The declaration file scripts/phase-50a/fixed-proof-executor.d.mts must be updated to match the new exported surface exactly.

TEST SEAM: the launch function and the liveness/verification probe stay injectable so tests can capture the ACTUAL options object and the ACTUAL signals production sends, and can force an unverifiable-containment case. Production passes nothing and gets the real implementations. The injection default must never be able to substitute a permissive stub into production.
credential_contract: Capture PHASE_50A_NPM_TOKEN from the ingress ONCE, into a single local binding, during the gate, and pass that binding to the launch seam. Refuse BEFORE the identity probe when it is missing, empty or whitespace-only, so nothing whatsoever launches — not even the probe.

Build every child environment by ENUMERATING the source environment's NAMES and SKIPPING both PHASE_50A_NPM_TOKEN and NODE_AUTH_TOKEN BEFORE any value is read. NEVER spread baseEnv and never delete-after-copy: the previous childEnv spread all of baseEnv and only then deleted the two names, which re-read both credential properties on every one of the thirteen child-environment constructions.

NODE_AUTH_TOKEN is added, from the captured binding, to the npm-ci entry ALONE, bound to that entry's LABEL rather than to a position or an argv guess. The identity probe and entries 2-12 receive NEITHER name, and neither do their descendants.

npm ci --ignore-scripts stays exactly as-is: it is load-bearing, keeping the repository's prepare lifecycle (and therefore the build) out of the one authenticated process tree. The explicit build remains a later entry holding neither name.
No token value may appear in a receipt, the identity banner, the published envelope, a refusal detail, a diagnostic, or any log line. Refusals name the VARIABLE, never its value.

concerns.description: F-04 NOT CLOSED — encoded credential query-parameter names bypass redaction. CREDENTIAL_PARAM_RE is built from the RAW literal names in CREDENTIAL_PARAMETERS and matched against the undecoded connection string, so a percent-encoded name never matches: `pass%77ord=<secret>` is decoded by pg (and by pg-connection-string) as `password` and is honoured as the credential, while redactConnectionString leaves the pair verbatim. The secret-bearing URI therefore still reaches diagnostics, error messages and log lines built from describeTarget(). The redactor deliberately never decodes (the comment at config.ts:124-127 states percent-encoded bytes inside the VALUE are covered without decoding) but the same reasoning does not hold for the NAME: the name is what selects the parameter for redaction. This is the same class of leak the sequence-83 audit raised, one channel deeper.

F-09/F-10 NOT CLOSED — fixed-descriptor validation is not bound to the supplied store/tool target. The validation establishes that SOME descriptor is well-formed but never proves that the descriptor validated is the same one the destructive path then uses, so an unrelated supplied store can reach destructive SQL (F-09), and an arbitrary database name can be registered as an issued target (F-10). The check and the use are two independent resolutions of the target rather than one bound identity; validating a fixed descriptor while accepting a caller-supplied store leaves the authority gap open.

F-14 NOT CLOSED — the required command-seam proof is vacuous. recordedStatements()/recordedStatementsAreReadOnly() observe a SYNTHETIC record: statements are appended by the verifier to its own module-level array rather than observed at the actual client.query call site, so the record is an assertion about what the code says it will run, not about what it ran. Nothing binds the recorded statements to the SQL actually issued to pg. Compounding this, the agree/mismatch proof can pass over an EMPTY record: recordedStatementsAreReadOnly() is vacuously true when no statement was ever appended, so a seam that records nothing satisfies the check. The proof therefore cannot fail in the way it is required to fail, and does not discharge the packet's command-seam requirement.

Proof/reporting inconsistencies. (a) The completion evidence reports nine changed entries where the substrate-to-head diff contains ten (cefe2b5..add1d1b is exactly 10 paths), so the report's own scope accounting does not reconcile with the tree. (b) The runbook carries edits outside the specifically named sections the packet authorised. Neither is a safety defect on its own, but both weaken the proof record that the closure claims rest on, and (a) understates the reviewed surface.

concerns.description: F-04 NOT CLOSED — parser-NORMALIZATION credential leak survives the sequence-93 fix. The fix moved the credential decision off the raw spelling onto the DECODED name: decodeParameterName applies decodeURIComponent (config.ts:153) to the raw query-parameter name, and isCredentialParameterName decides on that decoded, case-folded value. But pg-connection-string does NOT reach the parameter name by percent-decoding the raw text — it constructs a WHATWG URL and reads searchParams, and that construction NORMALIZES the name before any decoding happens. The two paths therefore still disagree, one layer above the layer the fix closed. Codex probed the target directly and against a real pg.Client: a parameter name carrying a bare LF, TAB or CR inside the word `password` (`pass<LF>word`, `pass<TAB>word`, `pass<CR>word`) is normalized by the URL/parser path to `password`, so the driver receives the supplied credential AS ITS PASSWORD, while decodeURIComponent leaves the name spelled with the raw control character, no entry of CREDENTIAL_PARAMETERS matches, and redactConnectionString leaves the credential verbatim in the URI. host.ts builds its diagnostics from describeTarget() -> redactConnectionString(this.config.connectionString), so the secret reaches diagnostics, error messages and log lines. This is the SAME class the sequence-89 audit rejected — redactor and parser disagreeing about which name is credential-bearing — reached through parser normalization rather than through percent-encoding.

(B1 / F-04 PARSER EQUIVALENCE) redactConnectionString decides WHICH query parameters are credential-bearing using the SAME EFFECTIVE NORMALIZATION AND PARSING SEMANTICS that determine whether pg / PostgreSQL actually receives a credential — not an independent approximation of them. The substrate decides on decodeURIComponent(rawName) (config.ts:153), but pg-connection-string reaches the name by constructing a WHATWG URL and reading searchParams, which NORMALIZES the name BEFORE any decoding: a name carrying a bare LF, TAB or CR inside a credential name normalizes to that credential name, so pg honours the value as the credential while the substrate redactor leaves it verbatim. THE FOLLOWING FIX CLASSES ARE EXPLICITLY FORBIDDEN: adding CR/LF/TAB (or any other) spellings; adding another normalization table; reproducing WHATWG normalization by hand; and extending regex or key-spelling heuristics. The implementation MUST instead derive its judgement from the SAME normalized parse representation the supported connection parser uses, so no future normalization or encoding behaviour can diverge from what the parser honours. The parser is reachable WITHOUT any dependency change: pg is a declared dependency, pg-connection-string is pg's own connection-string parser (pg/lib/connection-parameters.js line 7 requires it), and a pg.Client constructed from a connection string exposes the parser-derived credential — the implementer chooses the seam but MUST NOT edit package.json or package-lock.json. (B2 / FAIL CLOSED ON AMBIGUITY) When an input cannot be interpreted with sufficient certainty to establish which parts are non-secret — the parser throws, normalization is ambiguous, a name is undecodable (%ZZ), or the parsed representation cannot be aligned to the raw text being rewritten — the redactor WITHHOLDS or REDACTS the ambiguous sensitive portion rather than exposing it. It must still FAIL CLOSED WITHOUT THROWING: it runs inside error construction, so no input shape (malformed, truncated, non-URI, empty, non-string) may raise. (B3 / THE DECISIVE PROPERTY) IF the real supported parser derives a credential value from an input, THAT CREDENTIAL VALUE MUST NOT APPEAR IN ANY DIAGNOSTIC REPRESENTATION produced by the redaction path. This is a property over ALL inputs, not a case list, and it binds the PARSER-DERIVED value: note that the parser DECODES values (?password=sec%72et yields the credential `secret`), so the decoded value must not survive either, in any form. (B4 / DIFFERENTIAL ADVERSARIAL PROOF) A generated SEEK-DISAGREEMENT test must actively hunt parser/redactor divergence rather than enumerate known cases: it derives its cases from the real parser, and for every input where the parser derives a credential it asserts the value is absent from the redacted output. Coverage MUST include, and combine, at least: percent encoding; mixed case; CR/LF/TAB normalization; plus handling; DUPLICATE parameters; malformed escapes; and INTERACTIONS among those transformations. Duplicates deserve explicit care: the parser is LAST-WINS over searchParams, so `?pass<LF>word=A&password=B` yields B — the proof must not conclude that an earlier same-key value is therefore safe to print, because the surviving raw text still carries A. The test must be non-vacuous: assert a substantial checked count and a substantial parser-honoured count, so a generator that silently produces nothing fails. (B5 / SUBSTRATE-FAIL, FIX-PASS) The adversarial reproduction of Codex's counterexamples — a credential parameter name carrying a bare LF, a bare TAB and a bare CR inside a credential name — MUST FAIL against the substrate implementation and PASS after the fix, and both runs must be shown. A reproduction that passes on the defect proves nothing. concerns.description: F-04 NOT CLOSED — BLOCKING. src/straylight/storage/postgres/config.ts does not share the authoritative interpretation of the connection string; it TRANSCRIBES the parser's behaviour — the preprocessing step, the URL construction, the six-name credential classification and the case folding are re-implemented in the redaction path rather than obtained from the code that actually interprets the string. The transcription is not faithful to the real parser: pg-connection-string@2.14.0 also includes leading-slash socket handling and CASE-PRESERVING parameter assignment, and pg consumes the EXACT password the parser produced. Safe probes found conservative disagreements between the redactor and the parser on uppercase parameter keys and on socket forms. The generated oracle does not close this gap because it is NOT INDEPENDENT: it repeats the same six-name and lowercase assumptions as the code under test, so it misclassifies uppercase parameter names and names the parser ignores, and therefore cannot witness the disagreements it was built to detect. MUTATION PROOF FOR F-04 IS NON-VACUOUS.

F-09 NOT CLOSED — BLOCKING. openBoundProofStore both REGISTERS and EXPOSES the same mutable PostgresEstateHost object. A caller holding a GENUINE handle can therefore replace store.withClient after minting; the registry later returns that SAME mutated object, and emptySchema acts through it. The capability brand is thus not sufficient: authority is carried by an object that remains mutable after issuance, so post-mint alias redirection defeats the binding. The current tests do not cover this post-mint alias-redirection case. MUTATION PROOF DEFICIENT FOR F-09: mutation M2 creates an UNREGISTERED fake store rather than restoring the real post-mint alias defect, and it fails for a different reason than the defect under test — so M2 does not demonstrate that the F-09 proof would catch the actual defect.

F-14 NOT FULLY CLOSED — BLOCKING. The observation -> proof -> result/exit wiring is genuinely verdict-bearing: that part of the closure is real. The remaining defect is the classifier, which authorizes ARBITRARY BARE RELATIONS from syntax alone. A safe inert-client probe of `SELECT actor_id FROM side_effect_view` yielded proved=true, ok=true and exit status 0. Nothing in the audited surface proves such a relation non-destructive: there is no read-only transaction and no relation-semantics authority — a bare relation name that happens to parse as a SELECT is accepted as read-only on syntax alone, so a side-effecting relation passes the proof. MUTATION PROOF DEFICIENT FOR F-14: mutation M4 CHANGES CLASSIFIER BEHAVIOUR instead of restoring the rejected defect (observation disconnected from result/exit), so M4 does not demonstrate that the F-14 proof would catch the actual rejected defect.
